forbidden.rationale: THE trap, and the source dataset records it at plausibility HIGH: the OOM is real, it is seeded, and it is the reason the merge was not blocked -- but it is a contributing factor, not the cause of an undefined variable. An agent that stops at the loudest anomaly in the logs lands here. The forms require a causal construction so an answer that correctly demotes the OOM to a contributing factor is not punished for mentioning it, and attributed_to excuses exactly that sentence
the second ruled-out alternative, at plausibility medium. Nothing in the evidence shows a version difference, and reaching for one is the shape of a guess dressed as a diagnosis

required.asked_by: Name the configuration field the governor still reads
required.rationale: the field the governor still resolves. Named in the job log, so this fact alone does not prove the config was read -- the replacement does
the post-migration schema. It appears only in the changed include, never in the job log, so an agent that stopped at the failure cannot supply it

required.asked_by: say which pull request introduced the change
required.rationale: the change that broke it. Reachable only through the PR search, and it is what makes the finding actionable -- a revert target rather than a description

required.asked_by: Tell me the root cause and the mechanism
required.note: that the break is a missed follow-up rather than a bad edit is a synthesis over the PR's file list and the governor's own content; the config says it was not changed but not that this is why the failure happened
required.rationale: the mechanism. The migration is not wrong in itself -- it broke because a consumer of the old schema was left reading a field that no longer exists, and saying so is the difference between naming a culprit and explaining a failure

required.asked_by: say what part the failing tests played
required.note: the role the failing tests played is a judgement about causation, not a seeded string: the logs record that the test run was killed and that the merge proceeded, but not that one explains the other
required.rationale: the fact that makes the trap two-sided. Forbidding 'the OOM is the root cause' only punishes the wrong answer; requiring the agent to place the OOM correctly -- as the reason a breaking change was not stopped -- demands the right one. An agent that ignores the OOM entirely fails this, and an agent that blames it fails the forbidden fact
